描述_ZN: The Willow Sparrow" scroll, modern, painted by Xu Beihong, on paper with color, 131 cm in length and 38 cm in width.　　Self-titled: "Kindly accept the kind permission of the sage brother of Yipu. In the summer of the twenty-fourth year of Beihong." Inscription: "Wang Sun of the Eastern Sea" in white and long square seal.　　The twenty-fourth year refers to the twenty-fourth year of the Republic of China (1935), when Xu Beihong was 40 years old.　　As a painter of civilian origin, Xu Beihong had a simple outlook on life and art. He did not paint beautiful birds of prey with beautiful feathers or rare exotic birds, but liked to paint sparrows because "the sparrow is the most rustic, it is all ochre-brown, no bright colors, it even walks without posture, it is a rustic". In the eyes of Xu Beihong, sparrows because of the simplicity and lovely.　　The picture depicts the willow branches with shoots swaying and dancing in the spring breeze, attracting a flock of sparrows, they are flying flat, or sideways, or swooping, different forms, making the picture quite ornamental. People seem to hear their chattering and cheerful chirping, singing the bright spring light.　　The sparrows in the picture are colored with brushes and inked directly on the absorbent raw Xuan, showing the author's superior modeling ability and control of brushwork and ink. The body of the sparrow is painted with three or two strokes of ochre and light ink, and the hard wings, beak and claws are painted with heavy ink while still wet.
